title: Speed rational-rank certificate generation with primitive integer pivots
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The exact rational-rank certificate producer still used Fraction arithmetic for every forward-elimination entry after #6272 accelerated verification products. Use denominator-cleared primitive integer rows for pivot discovery, preserving the first-pivot policy and complete serialized certificate. This is verifier engineering; no new kappa or selected-frontier change.

On the unchanged #6272 48-by-64 rank-eight fixture, seven alternating fresh-process generate/save/check pairs reduce median local wall time from **727.3981 ms to 673.6825 ms (7.38%)**. All seven paired after times are lower; all 32 CLI commands, including warmups, pass with identical certificate bytes. This is one Windows/CPython workload, not an all-input or supplier speed claim.

## Task and overlap

Started from and refreshed against canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8, card `replay-runtime`, scope key `b1dd41940c60d240b47a` (refined scope). Checked live handoffs/Discussions and targeted all-state PR-body overlap. Local sparse-note/cache coverage is incomplete and explicitly recorded. #5789 supplies the interface; #6272 changes the product checker, while this change accelerates pivot discovery.

The [review note](https://github.com/josecarlosgonzalezroque-design/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e56d08c60910a4a635b708f26acbcc3326639dd5/docs/research/rational-rank-integer-pivots.md) records the proof, exact sources, overlap limits and open questions.

## Validation

- Eight rank tests pass normally and with `-I -O -W error`, including 154 new exact pivot/full-certificate comparisons against the Fraction policy. Existing independent minor-enumeration and damaged-certificate/input-byte controls remain.
- #6272's unchanged verifier passes normally and optimized: 591 complete certificate equalities, 802 product/mutation cases, 24 rejections.
- The selected binding-only baseline and `git diff --check` pass.
- The added opt-in benchmark and committed JSON receipt bind both source versions, fixture, parser and output hashes. Published tree `ca8b340c747b1b5dd752cd76a8e562b1e7f73687` exactly matches the staged local tree.

```sh
python -B -W error -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_rational_rank.py -v
python -I -O -W error -B tests/test_research_rational_rank.py -v
python -W error -B research/integer-rank-product-checks/verify.py
python -O -W error -B research/integer-rank-product-checks/verify.py
```

Environment: Windows 11 build 26300, CPython 3.12.10, 16 logical CPUs. No full supplier replay, complete multiplication proof, independent human review, or hosted CI success is claimed.

## Credit

Credit Ali Romman's #5789 interface, Nick Petalas's #6272 product optimization and benchmark fixture, and classical exact elimination. Prepared for josecarlosgonzalezroque-design with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, one agent; Apache-2.0. Frozen packages and the selected frontier are unchanged.

## Open next questions

Measure a named consumer's source-bound matrices before making a production-throughput claim. Separately compare high-rank matrices with unrelated denominators to assess peak memory and runtime; the present measurement establishes neither a worst-case bound nor a fixed-memory backend contract.
